account: DermaSensor of Miami makes a handheld device that shines light on a skin lesion and uses a machine learning algorithm to classify the reflected spectrum. In the DERM-SUCCESS pivotal study, 30 primary care physicians at 22 sites in the United States and Australia used it on 1,579 lesions in 1,005 patients. FDA reviewers report a device sensitivity of 95.5% for melanoma, basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma, against 83.0% for the physicians. Device specificity was 20.7%, against 54.2% for the physicians. In a companion reader study, 108 primary care physicians reviewed 50 lesion images with and without the device output. Their sensitivity rose from 82.0% to 91.4%, and their specificity fell from 44.2% to 32.4%. FDA granted the De Novo request on 12 January 2024. The reviewers note that the device will raise referrals of benign lesions and that patients with darker skin had limited representation.

ai_role.statement: In the reader study each physician judged every lesion with and without the device output, so the change in sensitivity is attributed to the device.
